newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MAN UTD V TOTTENHAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MAN UTD V TOTTENHAM.

text.p: Facts and figures for Sunday's English F.A. Cup third-round match between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford:

Manchester United: Formed 1878 as Newton Heath, changed name to Manchester United 1902. Major honours: European Champions 1968; European Cup Winners Cup winners: 1991. English League champions: 1908, 1911, 1952, 1956, 1957, 1965, 1967, 1993, 1994, 1996. F.A. Cup Winners: 1909, 1948, 1963, 1977, 1983, 1985, 1990, 1994, 1996. League Cup winners: 1992. Double winners: 1994, 1996
Record League Goalscorer: Bobby Charlton 199 goals, 1956-73
Most capped player; Bobby Charlton, England 106, 1958-70

Tottenham Hotspur: Formed 1882 as Hotspur FC, changed name to Tottenham Hotspur 1885. Major honours: European Cup Winners Cup winners: 1963; UEFA Cup winners 1972, 1984. English League champions: 1951, 1961. F.A. Cup winners: 1901, 1921, 1961, 1962, 1967, 1981, 1982, 1991. League Cup winners: 1971, 1973. Double winners: 1961
Record League Goalscorer: Jimmy Greaves, 220 goals, 1961-70
Most capped player: Pat Jennings, N.Ireland, 74, 1964-77
Note: In 1898-99 Manchester United were still known as Newton Heath

-- Manchester United (9 wins) and Tottenham (8) have won the Cup 17 times between them and been in a total of 23 finals but have never met each other in the Cup final. They came close in 1995 when they were kept apart in the semifinals. But while Manchester United beat Crystal Palace to reach the final, Tottenham lost to Everton in the other semifinal.

-- As well as meeting in the English League, F.A. Cup and League Cup, Tottenham and Manchester United have also clashed in Europe. In December 1963, Tottenham, the holders, played United in the first round of the European Cup Winners' Cup. Spurs won the first leg 2-0 at White Hart Lane but United won the tie 4-3 on aggregate after winning the second leg 4-1 at Old Trafford.

-- Tottenham goalkeeper Pat Jennings scored for Spurs direct from a clearance during their 3-3 draw against Manchester United in the 1967 Charity Shield match at Old Trafford. He later played for Arsenal against Manchester United, in the 1979 F.A. Cup final.
